extracted.intended_audience: Users of GAP (mathematicians, computational group theorists, and advanced students using the GAP computer algebra system)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for constructing and manipulating various group products and library groups in GAP, including function signatures, required input types/constraints, and semantics of embeddings/projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: SemidirectProduct: autgp must be automorphism group
rubrics_metrics.description: In the second variant, autgp must be a group of automorphism of N; it is a shorthand for SemidirectProduct(autgp, IdentityMapping(autgp), N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that (unless autgrp has been obtained by the operation AutomorphismGroup (40.7.1)) you have to test IsGroupOfAutomorphisms (40.7.2) for autgrp to ensure that GAP knows that autgrp consists of group automorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: SemidirectProduct: embeddings and projections semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: For a semidirect product P of G with N, calling Embedding(P,1) yields the embedding of G, calling Embedding(P,2) yields the embedding of N; calling Projection(P) yields the projection of P onto G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Embedding (32.2.11) and Projection (32.2.12) as described in the manual; examples show Image(Embedding(p,1)) and Embedding(p,2) usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: SubdirectProduct: definition and required homomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: SubdirectProduct(G, H, Ghom, Hhom) constructs the subdirect product of G and H with respect to the epimorphisms Ghom from G onto A and Hhom from H onto the same group A (the subgroup of G×H consisting of (g,h) with gϕ = hψ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the pull-back of the diagram with G, H and A. The function requires the two epimorphisms onto a common group A.

rubrics_metrics.name: SubdirectProduct: projection behaviour and non-embedding of factors
rubrics_metrics.description: For a subdirect product P, calling Projection(P,n) yields the projection on the n-th factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general the factors do not embed into a subdirect product; Projection returns the natural projection homomorphisms (see example usage).

rubrics_metrics.name: SubdirectProducts: compute all subdirect products up to conjugacy
rubrics_metrics.description: SubdirectProducts(G, H) computes all subdirect products of G and H up to conjugacy in the direct product of Parent(G) and Parent(H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subdirect products are returned as subgroups of this direct product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wreath product: domain is moved points (no fixed points)
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP considers the domain of a permutation group to be the points moved by elements of the group as returned by MovedPoints; it is not possible to have a domain including fixed points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus P = ⟨(1,2,3)⟩ and P = ⟨(1,3,5)⟩ result in isomorphic wreath products. If fixed points are desired form the wreath product G ≀ T with a transitive overgroup T of P and take the pre-image of P under the projection G ≀ T → T.

rubrics_metrics.name: WreathProduct: argument requirements and variants
rubrics_metrics.description: WreathProduct(G, H[, hom]) constructs the wreath product of G with H acting as a permutation group. If only two arguments are given, H must be a permutation group. If a third argument hom is given it must be a homomorphism from H into a permutation group; StandardWreathProduct(G,H) returns the wreath product for the (right regular) permutation action of H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When hom is given the action of the image on its moved points is considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wreath product: embeddings and projection semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: For a wreath product W = G ≀ P of degree n and 1 ≤ i ≤ n, Embedding(W,i) yields the embedding of G in the i-th component of the base group G^n; for i = n+1 Embedding(W,i) yields the embedding of P into W. Calling Projection(W) yields the projection onto the acting group P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Embedding (32.2.11) and Projection (32.2.12); examples illustrate Image(Embedding(w,3)) and Image(Projection(w), ...).

rubrics_metrics.name: WreathProductImprimitiveAction: imprimitive action construction
rubrics_metrics.description: WreathProductImprimitiveAction(G,H) constructs the wreath product of permutation groups G and H in the imprimitive action: if G acts on l points and H on m points this action will be on l·m points and will be imprimitive with m blocks of size l each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding and Projection operate as described for general wreath products; LargestMovedPoint can be used to inspect the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: WreathProductProductAction: product action construction
rubrics_metrics.description: WreathProductProductAction(G,H) constructs the wreath product in the product action: if G acts on l points and H on m points this action will be on l^m points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding and Projection operate as described for general wreath products; LargestMovedPoint and Size examples illustrate behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: KuKGenerators preconditions and output
rubrics_metrics.description: KuKGenerators(G, beta, alpha): if beta is a homomorphism from G into a transitive permutation group, U the full preimage of the point stabilizer and alpha a homomorphism defined on (a superset) of U, this function returns images of the generators of G when mapping to the wreath product (U^alpha) ≀ (G^beta) (Krasner-Kaloujnine embedding theorem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when constructing the explicit embedding guaranteed by the theorem; examples show constructing homomorphisms and calling KuKGenerators.

rubrics_metrics.name: ListWreathProductElement: decomposition and tests
rubrics_metrics.description: ListWreathProductElement(G, x[, testDecomposition]) returns [f1,...,fm,h] identifying the components of x in a wreath product G = K ≀ H, or fail if x cannot be decomposed. If omitted, testDecomposition defaults to true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If testDecomposition is true additional tests ensure the computed decomposition is correct: if K ≤ Sym(l) ensures x ∈ Sym(l) ≀ Sym(m) in the same action; if K ≤ GL(n,q) ensures x ∈ GL(n,q) ≀ Sym(m).

rubrics_metrics.name: WreathProductElementList: assemble element from components
rubrics_metrics.description: WreathProductElementList(G, list) returns the element x ∈ G identified by the tuple [f1,...,fm,h] for G = K ≀ H where fi ∈ K and h ∈ H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the NC (no-check) variant for faster construction when decomposition correctness is known.

rubrics_metrics.name: FreeProduct: constructing finitely presented free product
rubrics_metrics.description: FreeProduct(G[,H,...]) or FreeProduct(list) constructs a finitely presented group which is the free product of the given groups; if group arguments are not finitely presented, then IsomorphismFpGroup must be defined for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The operation Embedding (32.2.11) operates on this product; examples show FreeProduct([g,h,h]) usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding (for group products): general behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding(P, nr) returns the nr-th embedding in the group product P. The actual meaning of this embedding depends on the kind of product and is described in the product's manual section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the product-specific documentation (e.g., semidirect, wreath, free product) to interpret the embedding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection (for group products): general behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Projection(P, nr) returns the (nr-th) projection of the group product P. The actual meaning of the projection returned is described in the manual section for the appropriate product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projections give the natural homomorphisms from the product to its factors where defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group Libraries included with GAP
rubrics_metrics.description: When you start GAP it already knows several groups: some basic groups (cyclic, symmetric), classical matrix groups, transitive permutation groups (TransGrp package), small groups (SmallGrp), finite perfect groups, primitive permutation groups (PrimGrp), irreducible solvable subgroups of GL(n,q) (IRREDSOL), irreducible maximal finite integral matrix groups (dimension ≤31), and crystallographic groups (CrystCat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is usually no relation between groups in different libraries and a group may occur in different libraries in different incarnations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional installation of libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: A system administrator may choose to install all, only a few, or none of the libraries; some libraries mentioned may not be available on your installation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that availability of library data can vary across installations; code should not assume presence of particular libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: NoPrecomputedData option and data-library dependence
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP might use data libraries to speed up calculations (e.g., using classification to deduce isomorphism); this use is indicated by an info message of level 2 in InfoPerformance. To make a calculation independent of such data library use, call functions with the option NoPrecomputedData to turn these features off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turning off precomputed data can cause significantly longer calculations or even failure of certain calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic-group constructors accept optional filter argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions constructing infinite families of groups permit an optional filter argument (e.g., IsPermGroup, IsMatrixGroup, IsPcGroup) indicating the category in which the group shall be constructed. There is a default filter corresponding to a 'natural' way to describe the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every group can be constructed in every filter; theoretical restrictions apply (e.g., IsPcGroup only works for solvable groups) and methods may be available only for a few filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix-group constructors may accept field/ring hints
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain filters admit additional hints: groups constructed in IsMatrixGroup may be constructed over a specified field, which can be given as a second argument to the function that constructs the group; the default field is Rationals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the field/ring when the choice matters (examples show GL(4,3) vs GL(2,Integers), GL(3,Integers mod 12)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generator naming via generatorNames option
rubrics_metrics.description: For finitely presented groups (including polycyclic groups) generators are labelled by default with a letter and a number; the option generatorNames can influence naming: if it holds a string generators are named with that string and sequential numbers, if it holds a list of strings these are used in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show AbelianGroup([5,7]:generatorNames:="a") and use in AsSSortedList; provide a list long enough for the group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical groups: generator sources and invariant forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Generators for linear/symplectic/unitary/orthogonal groups are taken from cited sources (Tay87, IE94, KL90, RT98 etc.). For symplectic and orthogonal matrix groups the invariant bilinear form is stored in attribute InvariantBilinearForm; invariant sesquilinear form for unitary groups stored in InvariantSesquilinearForm; defining quadratic form stored in InvariantQuadraticForm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generators for semilinear groups are constructed from linear generators plus a field-automorphism generator; notes warn about differences in forms and references and mention Forms package compatibility for specifying forms explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms-package integration for specifying forms
rubrics_metrics.description: If version ≥ 1.2.6 of the Forms package is loaded, the desired form (sesquilinear/bilinear/quadratic) can be specified via the form argument (a matrix or form object) or by providing a group with stored invariant-form attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A given form determines d (and often q); an error is signalled if provided parameters do not fit the given form. Use this to create groups with a specific invariant form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective groups via OnLines/Action convenience
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the OnLines operation it is possible to obtain corresponding projective groups in a permutation action (e.g., to get a permutation action of PGL from GL via Action(..., OnLines)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only interested in the projective group as a permutation group and not in point correspondence, PGL(...) may be used instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific constructors and parameter constraints (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many specific group constructors are provided with default filters and parameter constraints: e.g., CyclicGroup(n) defaults to IsPcGroup unless n = infinity → IsFpGroup; AbelianGroup(ints) constructs C_{ints[1]}×...; ElementaryAbelianGroup(n) defaults to IsPcGroup; DihedralGroup(n) defaults to IsPcGroup unless n = infinity → IsFpGroup; MathieuGroup(degree) requires degree in {9,10,11,12,21,22,23,24}; SuzukiGroup(q) requires q a non-square power of 2 and defaults to IsMatrixGroup; ReeGroup constructs 2G2(q) where q = 31+2m for m a non-negative integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to each function's entry for exact defaults and examples (examples given for CyclicGroup, AbelianGroup, DihedralGroup, MathieuGroup, SuzukiGroup, ReeGroup).

rubrics_metrics.name: ExtraspecialGroup parameter form and filter defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: ExtraspecialGroup(order, exp) requires order of the form p^{2n+1} for a prime p and positive n; exp determined by allowable exponents or '+'/'-' signs (with special rules for p=2); default filter is IsPcGroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If p is odd admissible values of exp are p, p^2, '+', '-' etc.; examples show usage like ExtraspecialGroup(27,3) and ExtraspecialGroup(8,'-').
